newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Royale Belge rebounds five percent.
newsitem.headline: Royale Belge rebounds five percent.

text.p: Shares in Belgian insurance group Royale Belge rebounded five percent on Wednesday as investors bet again on the share benefiting from a merger between French parent UAP and rival AXA.
"It's related to the merger plan (between UAP and AXA)," a trader said.

By 1115 GMT the share was up 3.33 percent at 8,700 francs after touching 8,850 in earlier trade, with 62 million Belgian francs of the share traded. It was still below its year high of 9,350 francs, hit on March 17 in the wake of 1996 earnings news.
A merger pact between Royale Belge's French parent UAP with French rival AXA, creating AXA-UAP, will be completed formally in May.
Some have speculated this will lead to a shake up of all the combined group's units, with Royale Belge and AXA Belgium possibly also merging.
Royale Belge is presently controlled by Royale Vendome a holding company 25 percent owned by Groupe Bruxelles Lambert (GBL) and 75 percent owned by UAP.
One trader said, however, the insurer's rebound was a purely technical recovery from a fall on Tuesday linked to losses in New York.
"Royale Belge is a stock which is in a positive trend and liked by investors," the trader added, saying it would outperform the market in coming months.
